doc.title: Nick Mondello interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 19, 2022

title: Researching trumpeter Rocco Bene and the Philadelphia Cameo scene
summary: Rocco Bene was Philadelphia's lead trumpeter; Nick traces the Cameo-Parkway scene, Chubby Checker and the route to American Bandstand.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: That’s right. And how. I did a thing recently, this was another crazy project, on a trumpet player by the name of Rocco Bene. Now I happen to remember his name because in around Philadelphia, Rocco was like the guy, the lead trumpet player. So like in New York you had Bernie Glow, and in Philly you had Rocco, and of course in L.A. later on you had Al Porcino and Wayne Bergeron of course, all these great, great, great, tremendous, tremendous players. So I decided to research Rocco. And I knew about Rocco doing a lot of the Gamble and Huff produced Philadelphia International sides. But I didn’t know about the music scene in Philly in which Rocco played before all of the Cameo Parkway records, you know Chubby Checker and Little Eva, “Locomotion” and Fabian. But the crazy thing, you know you keep going you find out they all went to high school together. South Philadelphia High School. All of them. All right? And Cameo was upstairs from a jewelry store. The recording studio was upstairs and it was like bare bones. They had the microphone for the piano, was in the upright piano and all of these Cameo — Chubby Checker, right? That recorded for Cameo, and the guy that owned the jewelry store said, “You know I know a guy who is a producer on this relatively new T.V. show. Do you mind if I kind of mention it?” It turns out that the guy was friends with one of the producers on Dick Clark’s American Bandstand.
